Title: 11 Signs You're an AFC (Average Frustrated Chump) | Girls Chase
content:
Average Frustrated Chump: an ordinary guy, thwarted with women, falling for silly woman tricks. Here’s how to tell if you’re AFC – and what to do if so.

As I’ve been on social media (here’s our X account), I have come face to face with just how many frustrated, average men there are out there struggling with a lack of dating success.

That’s nothing new, of course. It’s always been this way. But Girls Chase has long served as kind of a bastion due to our large audience of savvy dudes vs. comparatively few very frustrated guys. After wading back onto social media though I’ve been smacked with guys who wouldn’t usually visit Girls Chase – or, if they found us, wouldn’t long stay to participate or read.

In recent years we’ve referred to various strains of frustrated men as ‘red pill’ (not all red pill men are frustrated, but many are), ‘black pill’, ‘incel’, ‘looksmaxx’; many different names.

Yet there’s another name that just as aptly captures all these various average, frustrated men under a single appellation: the Average Frustrated Chump (AFC).

Below I’ll help you realize if you are one – and if so, what to do!

 

We’re Bringing ‘AFC’ Back

The term Average Frustrated Chump, or AFC, dates to the early days of the seduction community. Ross Jeffries, founder of Speed Seduction® and one of the first modern seduction gurus, introduced the term AFC to differentiate between ordinary, woman-vexed men versus his students, the Speed Seducers.

Here’s an excerpt from Secrets of Speed Seduction, Ross’s 1994 book (and the earliest mention of the term ‘AFC’ I can find):

This brings us to a second key point that separates a Speed Seducer from the Average Frustrated Chump. You see, the AFC talks just to be flapping his lips, trying to be entertaining, or maybe, gulp, trying to get the girl to understand him. The Speed Seducer(and any good Master of Persuasion) knows that he must....

ALWAYS COMMUNICATE WITH A DIRECTION AND OUTCOME IN MIND!!!!

Already you can feel the difference between an AFC and a seducer. The AFC shoots his shot and hopes and prays. The seducer, on the other hand, has somewhere he’s taking things; some clear goal in mind.

When I set up Girls Chase I left a lot of the old seduction community jargon behind to make this place more accessible to a wider audience. That definitely worked; at the time of this article we’ve reached over 64 million men since opening our doors. We’ve achieved mass appeal.

But after years of dealing with guys calling themselves all sorts of things while manifesting the SAME frustration with women and the dating game, and now after getting a look at what passes for ‘rizz’ on social media (i.e., guys making THE most AVERAGE approaches in the WORLD), I’ve realized Ross’s phraseology here is simply the best.

Let’s start calling a spade a spade: if a guy is average (in his behavior, and especially in WOMEN’S eyes!) and frustrated, and he does not know WHY or HOW to fix his romantic results, he is an Average Frustrated Chump!

But let’s say you aren’t sure if you fall into the AFC camp or not (or whether one of your buddies might). How can you tell who’s an AFC from who’s not?

Below, I’ve put together a handy list that runs you through the signs a man is average, frustrated, and a bit too much of a chump with women and romance.

 

#1: He Attributes Dating Success to ‘Luck’

Whether he believes:

Romantically successful men won the ‘genetic lottery’, no doubt cleaning up because of their good looks, height, intelligence, or some other trait,

Or that romantic success stories luckily stumbled into the right early mentors or experiences to teach them ‘game’ while young and impressionable,

Or that successful romantics are just guys really good at “getting lucky”, being in the right place at the right time to end up with a girl in their bed,

It is all the same:

This is a guy who thinks “the universe” picks and chooses romantic victors, and that there is NOTHING he can do about it!

Men like this are average (at least in women’s eyes), they are frustrated, and because this belief keeps them trapped in inaction, they are CHUMPS!

 

#2: He Blames Society for His Lackluster Love Life

This one is all the rage right now.

It’s because of all the attention women receive on apps, you see.

It’s all their thirsty male followers on social media validating them like crazy.

It’s the fawning feministic media praising women at every turn.

THAT’S why women behave so entitled! THAT’S why they aren’t into him!

Never mind the fact that a lot of women have tiny social media profiles or none at all… and most women don’t use dating apps. Somehow it bleeds through anyway even to these women and makes them blind to the AFC’s romantic value!

Just like the men who attribute successful men’s success to ‘luck’, those who attribute romantic successes and failure to society seek to externalize responsibility.

But when you externalize responsibility, you condemn yourself to ever being average; you condemn yourself to frustration; and above all, you condemn yourself to being (and staying) a chump!

 

#3: He’s Frustrated with Women’s Resistance (or Disinterest)

Everybody gets frustrated when things don’t go his way.

Average Frustrated Chumps however get a much bigger helping of this than successful seducers do. For the AFC:

Women resist him at every turn

Women show active disinterest in him

Women block his moves and reject him

… and he just does not know why!

No matter how special he may feel, there’s a part of him that knows that women see him as ‘average’. This frustrates him to no end – but without a roadmap to figuring it out, he’s stuck being a chump.

 

#4: He Has Long, Involuntary Periods of Celibacy

If a guy goes a year or more without getting laid, he’s probably an AFC.

(occasionally a seducer will have a ‘low period’ where he barely goes out and barely meets women and may have a dry spell for that reason. But for highly skilled seducers this is rare)

If you’re an even halfway decent seducer, dry spells are not a big problem. Even if you’re low momentum, you just go out and hit your girl avenues harder and keep at it till you get over the hump and pull a new girl to bed.

The Average Frustrated Chump has no such ability.

For the AFC, if he has no girls around, he has no girls around, and there’s not a whole lot he can do about that.

Every single guy in the incel (involuntarily celibate) community is an AFC. (or, perhaps more aptly in their cases, a bAFC or wbAFC – “below AFC” or “way below AFC”)

But a lot of regular ol’ dudes who go through prolonged dry spells are AFCs too.

They may not be as bad off as the ‘avowed incel’ types (bAFC/wbAFC), but nevertheless:

The are average, they are frustrated, and they (sad to say it) are chumps!

 

#5: He’s Looking for a Dating “Magic Pill”

Your average Frustrated Chump isn’t looking for a process or a method to follow.

He’s looking for a “quick fix”: that one mindset tweak, appearance upgrade, or magic set of words that will make girls’ panties DROP (or the girl of his dreams fall in love!).

This “quick fix”, “magic pill” mentality keeps AFCs jumping from one mantra to another, one cockamamie idea to the next.

First it’s dating apps; then when that doesn’t work it’s the latest trendy sporty activity; then after no dice there, it’s going to parties to try out the latest pickup line.

Even though any of these venues CAN work just FINE for a dedicated seducer with a good process, they’re all equally bad for the AFC, because he’s mostly hoping to get lucky – yet he mostly does not.

 

Quick Intermission: How to Stop Being an AFC
Get free of being an AFC.

If you’re reading this and find yourself saying, “Oh no – I’m an AFC!” don’t worry – there is a cure.

If you’re new to Girls Chase, you can familiarize yourself with some of our most important, foundational articles here. These will get you up-to-speed and start the epiphanies coming.

If you’d like a more tailored experience, you can take the free Diagnostic Quiz and complete the 30-day workbook I’ll email you with your results. (I’ll also send you my 7-day free mini course as an added thanks for signing up)

If you’re chomping at the bit and totally ready to dive into an end-to-end system, then either pick up my best-selling seduction handbook How to Make Girls Chase OR start using my “get the girl in one easy-to-get date” One Date System (which teaches you to expertly wield my seriously overpowered SAC attraction model).

Any/all of these will get you well on the way to shedding that AFC chrysalis and emerging as a beautiful seductive lepidopteran – one women cannot wait to have land on their petals and sip of their sweet, sweet nectar!

End intermission. Onward with our 10 Signs a Guy Is an AFC.

Next up: #6 – sweeping generalizations.

 

#6: He Buys Into Sweeping Generalizations About Women

All these phrases, while not all in agreement, have something in common:

“Women don’t want sex. They want relationships.”

“All women are sluts.”

“Women only care about a man’s looks.”

“Women only care about a man’s bank account.”

“Women only care about a man’s social status.”

“No woman is loyal.”

“Hot women aren’t worth the work.”

“All women are like that.” (AWALT)

“Girls don’t actually like bad boys. It’s just a meme.”

“Women take advantage of good guys.”

What these phrases have in common is they are sweeping generalizations of women that exhibit the man’s lack of nuanced perspective – and, very often, his bitterness toward girls.

Read most of those sweeping generalizations and you can feel the frustration. Guys who express generalizations like this don’t want them to be true, yet tell themselves they are:

Men who say all women are sluts are complaining because they’ve been unable to find a girl who isn’t a slut.

Men who say no women are loyal are complaining because they’ve failed to find a loyal woman.

Men who say “all women are like that” are complaining because they’ve failed to find a woman who is not “like that.”

These men want something they’re unable to find/get, making them highly frustrated.

Read the rest of those and you can feel the chump-ness. “Women don’t want sex…” Sure buddy. Keep telling yourself that. “Girls don’t like bad boys.” Uh-huh.

Regardless whether the man leans more ‘frustrated’ or more ‘chump’, if he hews to sweeping generalizations about women, he is an Average Frustrated Chump!

 

#7: The Idea of Treating Social Skills as Skills Feels Alien

Social skills to an AFC are something you either have or you don’t; you’re either born with them or you’re not. The idea of treating these skills as skills… i.e., things you must work at over time to develop… is utterly foreign to him!

Never in his life has he actively tried to:

Alter his appearance to see how that affects the way others treat him.

Improve his conversation to make himself more interesting or effective.

Refine his ability to provide value to others to make him like them more.

Learn how to consistently close people to build the relationships he wants.

Develop other basic social skills that allow him to achieve what he wants socially.

Even though the word ‘skills’ is RIGHT THERE inside the term ‘social skills’, the AFC still doesn’t see it. It’s built into the term, yet it does not register.

Because he does not view his socializing as a skill-based process, his social abilities remain locked away, unable to blossom… and he remains just an Average Frustrated Chump.

 

#8: He Does Stuff for Women Without Receiving Much/Anything Back

Mind your investment scales, young one. It’s not how much you invest in her; it’s how much she invests in you!

Men who:

Do too much for girls
Spend too much on girls
Give too much time to girls
Pay too much attention to girls
Over-accommodate girls in any way

… while not receiving remotely comparable investment back from the girl always end up frustrated that their efforts are not rewarded, typically without realizing just how average the efforts they’re making seem to the girl – all of which comes together to make these poor men chumps!

 

#9: He Claims a Man Who Sleeps with Women ‘Ruins’ Them

How do you know a man does not get tail?

An easy one is if he thinks the men getting tail are ‘ruiners of women’.

This belief is just impotent self-interest wrapped up in a kind of ‘social good’ framing.

I’ve read a lot of the writing of great men over the past 3,000 years. Many of them lived during times of civilizational decadence, when marriage and childbirth were on the decline and casual sex was rampant. I’ve never encountered a great man blaming individual playboys who slept with women for this. Some of them blame women for it, but more of them blame the overall decline of the society for it (systemic effects). No great man has ever said, “It’s those amoral playboys, taking advantage of our pure princesses!”

Some Average Frustrated Chumps try to shame women into ‘behaving’: “women need to stop slutting it up and become mothers again!” Other AFCs try to shame sexually successful men into ‘behaving’: “men need to stop corrupting women by sleeping with them sans commitment!”

Across the board, however, these efforts are utterly impotent; the AFC is an outsider commenting on the happy hanky-panky of women and sexually successful men. He’s standing outside the cabin the women and seducers are lovemaking in, banging on the window panes and shouting for them to stop as they ignore him.

Sexually successful men know that women, just like female animals of every other species, are attracted to desirable mates and will pursue pairings with them. They are not following rigid societal rules (most of which have been laid out in the past by prior generations of AFCs). The Don Juan and the woman are members of the Secret Society – something the Average Frustrated Chump does not even know exists.

 

#10: He’s Trying to Pass a Non-Dating Milestone to Get Girls

Building a fit, healthy, well-muscled body is a great and admirable goal.

Developing a successful business or career with a comfortable bank account is smart to do.

Climbing to a prominent place in society where you are known, respected, and possess great influence is laudable.

But if you do any of these things primarily to get women, then you are AFC!

Any roundabout way of trying to get women is the AFC approach. AFCs are too afraid to expose themselves to frequent rejection and uncomfortable social situations. So, instead, they lock themselves ‘in the lab’, hunkered down in ‘monk mode’, and tell themselves the fantasy that once they build it, the women will come:

“Once I’m a musclebound HULK, girls will be all over me!”

“Once I’m as rich as Bill Gates, the pussy train will never stop!”

“Once I’m world famous, you won’t be able to SCRAPE women off me!”

Even if the guy is successful at achieving all he hopes in his given focus area (and many guys are not ultimately all that successful at it; it takes a lot of work to become Arnold Schwarzenegger!), he will generally not have been working on his social or seductive skills in the meantime.

When such a man emerges from his cocoon into the world again, he discovers that girls are only mildly interested in his bulging muscles or impressive career. They might act intrigued for a few minutes, then they get bored and wander away. All that to impress girls for a couple of minutes. Ouch.

Success and attractive qualities are worth cultivating if you want to cultivate them… but if you want to get GIRLS, you must focus not on ‘other qualities’ but on girls!

Focusing on anything other than what specifically it takes to court and keep women condemns a man to (rich/famous/muscular/other useful-but-tangential stuff) Average Frustrated Chump Land.

 

#11: He Frequently Falls for Girls He Hasn’t Slept with Yet

She’s so perfect and amazing.

He can’t help imagining his potential bright future with her!

Everything about her tickles his senses and sings to his heart.

There’s just one thing: he hasn’t even slept with her yet. She’s not his!

READ MORE: Can't Stop Thinking About Her? Here's Why You Need to Meet More Girls

Meet MORE girls!

If a man falls in love with girls before he’s even slept with them, he is an AFC. Why does this make him an AFC? Well, first off, because dudes who actually get girls don’t fall in love with them before they get together. They move too fast and have too many other female options to be falling for women they aren’t actually together with.

But perhaps more importantly, this makes him an AFC because when you fall in love with girls before sleeping with them, most of the time (particularly in fast-paced, competitive mating markets) you will not get them.

You tread too cautiously, miss escalation windows, then let attraction expire and miss the boat with her. Some other guy comes along who takes her far less seriously, isn’t all head-over-heels in-love with her, gets her, and you are out.

The guy who falls in love with girls he isn’t together with yet ends up perplexed, wondering why this girl he was so in-love with got with another guy and NOT him.

It’s so frustrating, and he feels like such a chump… because, unfortunately, he is.

He’s an Average Frustrated Chump – and this is just how dating is for him!

 

Break the Cycle of Frustration

Lots of men are Average Frustrated Chumps. Most men are! That’s why the term is ‘Average’, not ‘Unusual’, ‘Rare’, or ‘Uncommon’. It may be unfortunate to be an AFC, but it’s by no means out of the ordinary.

If a man is an AFC, should he stay an AFC? Most AFCs end up in relationships sooner or later… even if they DO settle, and even if they DO tend to have Average Frustrating Relationship Problems. But hey – if a guy just doesn’t have the energy or the drive to leave being an AFC behind, there’s no ‘AFC Police Squad’ that’s going to come and arrest him for the crimes of being average, frustrated, and a chump.

What if he doesn’t want to be an AFC though? What if he wants to be a sexy seducer – or even just a solidly cool dude with a certain degree of competence with the fairer sex?

Then in that case, it’s time to leave aside being an Average Frustrated Chump and learn the ins and outs of women and attraction.

You’re at THE right place to do that.

You can:

Read the articles on the Girls Chase “Start Here” page

Take the Girl Q Diagnostic Quiz and go through the free book + free email course

Buy my detailed seduction & attraction handbook, How to Make Girls Chase

Begin my flagship training program One Date & The Dating Artisan to achieve absolute dating mastery

The road is open to you, the sun is shining, the grass is green, and the wind is at your back.

There is nothing forcing you to remain an AFC.

You, like many men who’ve come before you, can learn to understand women, what makes them tick, what buttons to push with them, and what to do to get the girls you want into the relationships you desire.

You can be the man who, like Ross’s Speed Seducers, always has a direction in mind with everything he says or does, and often arrives at it, women in-hand.

When you’re ready to begin, all the resources are right there – success with sexy women awaits.

Your Friend,

Chase Amante

Title: Getting Tested for STIs: The Active Dater's Guide | Girls Chase
content:
If you’re actively taking on new bedfellows, you should be testing for STIs. How should you test these? Where to do it? When? It’s all in this guide.

Hey guys. I hope you are doing well.

Today, I’ll continue my discussion about sexually transmitted infections (STIs). In this article, I will cover STI testing and share the information I have gathered over the years through clinic visits, conversations with specialists, and readings from scientific papers. I encourage you to visit a clinic to learn more from healthcare professionals, and while you’re there, consider getting tested. Please remember that this post is not a substitute for professional advice from certified healthcare providers.

 

Testing 101
Testing is important. Don’t skip it.

For me, testing is the holy grail when it comes to STIs. Whenever you have unprotected sex, you should get tested. The cure to STI worries is through testing. Testing is the best way to ensure good sexual health. You can eliminate the curable infections and drastically reduce the chance of getting the non-curable ones. Note that getting rid of the curable infections decreases contracting the non-curable ones. For more, see part one of this series. It helps ensure your good sexual health and protects others.

Testing is THE magic word. It can be scary, but honestly, it is less frightening than you think:

You may not have anything (likely), and your mind will be at ease.

If you have something, it is usually curable (like gonorrhea or chlamydia).

It is less likely that you have syphilis. If you do, you want to eradicate it as quickly as possible. The treatment is typically three injections in your backside over one month.

It is more unlikely that you could have hepatitis C. If you do, you want to eliminate it because serious complications can develop. This involves one to two months of well-tolerated anti-virals.

It’s very unlikely, but you may contract HIV. This is the scary one that I will devote a section to below.

HIV is a severe disease that, if left untreated, leads to AIDS and early death. However, if you have access to treatments, you will not get AIDS, you will not die earlier, and it will not affect your life expectancy. You will also not be contagious after taking the usual treatment for a certain amount of time (usually two to three months). A doctor will sample your blood regularly, and you are not contagious if your doctor cannot detect any virus. You can resume your sex life and not put others at risk. If you are unsure about these details, I encourage you to talk to a healthcare professional.

However, the price for having a normal sex life with HIV is that you must take pills daily and get your blood tested often to ensure treatment works and to know whether you are contagious or not.

I do not want to trivialize HIV. Do your best to protect yourself. However, one also must be informed and look at it with some nuance: it is not the end of the world.

Untreated HIV is not only very contagious, as you put others at serious risk, but extremely dangerous for you. The more you wait, the worse your prognosis is. HIV will not damage your system immediately, but if you wait too long, it may cause irreversible damage. If you take the correct treatment before it causes damage, you can mitigate this.

The bottom line is that you are better off by getting tested. Here is why:

If you get tested for HIV, you will clear your mind and know that you don’t have it, or find out you have it, and significantly reduce its effects by getting treatment.

If you do not get tested, you will keep wondering and worrying, and if you are positive, you contaminate others and eventually destroy your immune system.

So, get tested.

 

Where to Test?
Specialized STI clinics are an excellent choice.

Visit your general practitioner. If a doctor is judgmental, change doctors. If your doctor is not judgmental and you are comfortable with them, they can do the testing or prescribe a battery of tests for you. This is totally fine.

I can understand that this can be uncomfortable for some. If so, head to a specialty clinic. They are usually anonymous and free. Most importantly, they are highly specialized.

The latter is the reason why I prefer them to my doctor. Specialty clinic professionals have cutting-edge knowledge, and aside from testing and treating, their role is to educate others. It’s how I acquired much of my STI knowledge. Ask them in-depth questions. They usually know the answers; if they don’t, they know someone who does. They can give you the latest facts, which can really help if you are worried. Be open and talk with them.

The vibe there can sometimes be shady, and the clientele can be questionable. But this is good because you will feel more comfortable opening up knowing you have many people in that waiting room who are likely much more hardcore than you are. You are likely not like them and trust me, I know. I had a friend who was an HIV specialist at a clinic. The stories he relayed were at the next level (note that he never shared patient details or anything that could out them). So, you can feel comfortable with these healthcare providers.

Some general practitioners are not up-to-date on infectious diseases like the specialty clinics are. This is because they are not specialists. You cannot blame them. The issue is that they can give you outdated details. One doctor told me I had to wait two to three months before testing for HIV, and that’s not correct today. It may have been valid years ago. So, I recommend going to a specialty clinic.

The benefit of going to a general practitioner is the shorter waiting time. The waiting time in free public clinics is quite long. If you have limited time, go to your GP. Unless you already have a good foundation about STI facts, I recommend heading to the clinics and using the visit to educate yourself thoroughly. Once you know the drill, you can take shortcuts through your GP (you will likely have to pay).

 

What to Test For?
All the good ones.

What should you ask the specialist to test you for? Here are the MUSTS.

Chlamydia

Gonorrhea

Syphilis

Ask for a hepatitis B test if you are not vaccinated. They can test to see if you have been vaccinated, so healthcare professionals can discard a positive test if vaccinated.

You can ask for a test for HIV-1 and HIV-2. (Most tests today test for both. I have not encountered a test for only one.)

If you can, test for hepatitis C and mycoplasma. If they offer it, say yes; if they don’t, request it. Typically, clinics only test for hepatitis C once yearly, but sometimes, asking will suffice for testing regularly. You may omit mycoplasma if you are asymptomatic, but if they offer it, get the test.

Note that specialty clinics will likely not test for herpes (HSV) and warts (HPV) unless you have an outbreak. If you do, they might diagnose you from visual inspection and take a sample (scrubbing) for testing. However, they may not test unless you have symptoms.

You can test for herpes through a blood test to see if you have the virus. However, your GP will do this and not the specialty clinic. I do not recommend this as a routine test unless a professional requests it. The test results may be insignificant. You are likely positive (most people have herpes), and if you are, there is not much you can do, and there’s no guarantee that you will experience outbreaks. This may be a pointless test.

The mononucleosis test, which one can catch from sleeping around (but even from drinking from other people’s cups), is unlikely to be offered by an STI clinic. You will have to go to your general practitioner. There is no need to test for it unless you are symptomatic.

 

When to Test?
Checking at the right time interval is crucial.

Here are the incubation periods for each STI:

Chlamydia: 7–21 days (Most clinics suggest testing after around 7-10 days)

Gonorrhea: 1–14 days (most clinics suggest a testing after around 7 days)

Syphilis: 10–90 days (most clinics suggest testing after one month, and again after three months if symptomatic, and regularly test if sexually active)

Hepatitis B: 21–150 days (most clinics will suggest testing after four weeks of exposure and frequent testing if sexually active and unvaccinated)

Hepatitis C: 10 to 90 days (most clinics suggest testing after one month and suggest retesting if sexually active or at risk)

HIV: 14 to 90 days (most clinics suggest testing after six weeks; this is the recommendation in Europe)

There are debates about these time windows; variations between countries and clinics will occur. Here are the guidelines from the CDC: https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/yellowbook/2024/posttravel-evaluation/sexually-transmitted-infections

If you test before the incubation window, chances are that your test will be a false negative. It may indicate negative, but you are infected, giving you a false sense of security.

Here are a few good rules of thumb:

If you have had unprotected sex and want to get tested, do it after six weeks. Most tests are reliable after six weeks. If, after intercourse, you test yourself after six weeks, you can be rest assured that you are okay.

If you have symptoms like pain in your testicles, pain while urinating, or discharge from your penis, see your doctor and get examined and tested, even before six weeks. You likely have gonorrhea or chlamydia. And if you don’t, you may still have a non-sexually transmitted urinary tract infection, which still needs treatment.

If you get a rash or round, open sores in your pubic area, get looked at and tested. It may be syphilis.

Cold-like symptoms may be symptoms of HIV and do not warrant special attention. Just get tested after six weeks unless the symptoms are unbearable, like a high fever.

 

No Shortcuts

There are no home kits for HIV testing and no home test for chlamydia. Some that you buy online are questionable. Even those you see in pharmacies are less precise than lab tests. So, forget about other options as they are unreliable. Do you want to get a false negative, or worse, a false positive HIV result from a home kit? It’s not worth it.

Do lab tests through a healthcare provider. No shortcuts.

When getting a clinic HIV test, request the fourth-generation AB/AG test that tests for antibodies and antigens. This test is more reliable with fewer false negatives, and you can test earlier. The “wait two months before testing” for HIV is for older test generations. Most clinics offer the newer, fourth-generation test.

Beware of “rapid tests,” like saliva or quick tests from drawing blood from a finger. Only get the needle-in-the-arm tests performed in a clinic or laboratory.

 

What About HIV Testing?

If you have a serious HIV scare, it can be difficult to wait six weeks. The worries may be unbearable. I have good news, however. Waiting six weeks is ideal for HIV testing, and the reliability is close to 100% (Remember that 0% and 100% do not exist in medicine). But, I can live with 99% after 44 days, and most medical professionals will conclude that you do not have HIV and will not need retesting. Testing again is warranted if doctors consider you at high risk for exposure, like if you had sex with someone who just got diagnosed positively. Remember, the six-week window applies only to fourth-generation AB/AG needle-in-the-arm tests.

If you cannot wait six weeks, you can get tested after two weeks. You may do this if you think you are infected, as the antigen (p24) shows up on blood tests after approximately two to three weeks. They may decrease after four to eight weeks, and it’s why the fourth generation also tests for antibodies. If infected, positive results appear after three to four weeks and stay detectable for the rest of your life. This means you could detect HIV after two weeks with a reasonable success rate and almost perfectly detect HIV after six weeks.

Testing after two to three weeks is okay if you want to calm your nerves and get an idea of where you are. If you are negative after two to three weeks, you likely do not have HIV.

However, this will not clear you. A test after two to three weeks is not enough. It can give you a good indicator. If you are negative, you likely do not have HIV, but you cannot tell for sure. Retest after four weeks to be certain. At this point, you can move on.

Note: You can technically test for HIV after seven to ten days with an RNA Quantitative (viral load) test. These tests are expensive and not reliable for diagnosis. Doctors typically administer these to monitor HIV patients already diagnosed. However, if your paranoia is at the next level, you can do an antigenic test and an RNA test after two weeks. If both are negative, you can be reasonably sure you do not have HIV. However, you should still get retested after four weeks.

For more details, see https://i-base.info/guides/testing/what-is-the-window-period and https://www.aidsmap.com/about-hiv/what-window-period-hiv-testing

 

Parting Words
You’ll feel a lot more confident when you know you’re in the clear.

Whenever you have unprotected sex, you should test yourself after six weeks (and earlier if you experience symptoms). I usually advise anyone to test themselves at least once a year.

For sexually active men, I advise testing three to four times a year, usually three to four months apart, but test right away whenever you have symptoms and then test more often. I have a routine test every three to four months. Most health authorities recommend this time frame for at-risk groups. These groups include men who have sex with men, prostitutes, drug users, and transgender people. However, although less discussed, sexually active heterosexuals also fall within this category. So, it is better to get tested four times a year.

My recommendation to you is to get tested at a clinic soon if you haven’t been tested in a while, using the occasion to discuss your sexual history with an expert and create a plan for how often you should get tested (they will likely suggest a less stringent protocol than mine). Utilize those health professionals to develop the best plan for your sexual health. This is the way to go about it.

It is better to test too much than too little. If you are unsure whether you should get tested, do it. It’s that simple.

Stay safe,

Alek

Title: Tactics Tuesdays: Self- vs. Other-Pointing | Girls Chase
content:
Pointing at yourself or others as you set emotional frames anchors those emotions to the pointee. Can you use this in seduction? You absolutely can…

A recent study examined US President Donald Trump’s use of pointing to connect with his audience. The study authors note

Results show that (i) inward points are associated with first-person references; (ii) outward points are associated with second person and third person/object references; (iii) downward points are associated with locative expressions; (iv) looping marks plurality and inclusiveness and (v) internal complexity is associated with expressions of number, time, sequence and comparison.

The authors further note that “Trump uses pointing in the kinesic performance of right-wing populism to entertain his audience, to engage with them more directly, to steer their attention and to align himself with them as a man of the people.”

While academia may just be catching up, the use of pointing has been with us since before we were human (apes, for instance, are known to point).

And one place we’ve long paid attention to the usefulness of the point is in neurolinguistics programming.

 

NLP and Pointing

In neurolinguistics programming (NLP), pointing is used to anchor emotions to specific targets.

As a very basic example, if I say to you that, “You have been very bad,” while pointing at you, you are going to tend to feel much more singled out than if I say, “You have been very bad,” but do not point at you. The addition of the nonverbal element (i.e., pointing right at you) amplifies the message and strengthens the emotional impact. You feel much more harshly judged when I point at you than when I don’t – even if my words, facial expression, tone of voice, and all my other body language is the same.

NLP uses a few core pointer motions, including:

Self-point: when the speaker points at himself.

Other point: when the speaker points at someone else (such as his listener or another party).

The study I referenced at the start of the article also mentions downward pointing to reference a location (“Here, today”) and gestural loops to communicate inclusiveness or multiples of something (“We’re all in this together”).

Because of the way we anchor emotions to targets, pointing at something serves a purpose of telling your viewer and listener where to anchor the emotion you create.

So for instance, if we’re talking and I say something about “very successful people” and at the same time gesture toward myself, your subconscious mind will form an association between “very successful person” and me, Chase Amante. If I then say “people who want more success” and gesture in your direction, you will feel the emotion anchoring to yourself of “I am someone who wants more success.” I can repeat this gestural anchoring more times as we converse and further strengthen the emotional anchor.

This might sound minor, but in fact it is a very powerful tactic. Human interpersonal liking and communication relies primarily on body language. Because our brains contain mirror neurons, when we see someone do something our brains internally model the action, strengthening the pathways between that emotion and its target in the brain. When I point to myself while stating something, you internally point to me too as I state that thing. When I point at you while stating something else, you internally also point at yourself as I state that other thing.

As PsyPost notes

Outward pointing created a dynamic of direct engagement, drawing the audience into the conversation while also enabling Trump to physically single out targets for praise, criticism, or ridicule.

Conversely, inward pointing, directed towards Trump’s own body, was strongly associated with first-person singular pronouns (“I,” “me,” “my”). This occurred particularly when Trump was emphasizing his personal qualities, his commitment to his supporters, or his differences from other politicians.

The use of pointing cements the emotion being conveyed, anchoring it deeper in the mind, or connecting the speaker more firmly to his listeners.

Linguistics professor Christopher Hart, the author of the study, says “Self-pointing is functionally redundant so might not be expected to occur frequently but Trump uses them to contrast himself with other politicians. Self-points in other contexts do not normally make contact with the chest but Trump’s self-points do make contact with the chest the majority of the time. This might imply sincerity and allow Trump to connect with his audience on an emotional level.”

I highlight the note about ‘functional redundancy’ – he’s right, from a totally detached functional perspective, referring to yourself verbally while at the same time pointing at yourself seems redundant. Why not just use the words and skip the gesture?

The reality of course is that gestures are not functionally redundant; rather, they serve a purpose of highlighting, emphasizing, and directing the thoughts and emotions expressed to more firmly anchor them in the brain.

This works even if the target of the emotion is not named.

 

Using Pointing to Anchor Emotions

There’s an old good video from the BBC where interviewer Louis Theroux watches as Ross Jeffries, the founder of the NLP-based Speed Seduction and godfather of the modern seduction community, demonstrates NLP seduction. In the video, Ross uses liberal amounts of pointing to anchor emotions as he seduces a woman he’s just met.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xn_oqEOtLYU

How does that work? How is Ross able to generate emotions in a woman just by saying things then pointing at or touching her? Via the power of pacing and leading plus anchoring.

There are a variety of ways to use self- and other-points in seduction, not all of them direct.

A classic example is when you self-point while describing some characteristic you want a woman to anchor to you in her mind. For instance, if you are talking and say “some guys are just very exciting” while gesturing subtly toward yourself, the girl you’re talking to may not even consciously register your self-point – but subconsciously, her mind anchors the concept of “very exciting guy” to you.

Here are a few examples of frames and emotions it’s useful to anchor to yourself with a subtle self-point:

“The kind of guy you fall in love with”

“Someone who’s a bit mysterious and hard to figure out”

“Someone you just feel butterflies when you’re around”

“A man you feel an irresistible attraction to”

So for instance, if you’re talking to a girl, once she is hooked and is in a receptive mode with you, you might ask her, “Hey, let me ask you this: have you ever met a man you feel an irresistible attraction to?” while using a self-point. If you’re looking deep in her eyes as you say this, she won’t consciously register your self-point; she’ll be focused on your eyes and the emotion you’re discussing with her. Yet subconsciously, the emotion anchors to you, and she begins to feel you are a man she has some kind of irresistible attraction to.

The effect is subtle, but the effect is noticeable.

Obviously, if you anchor a bunch of frames and expectations to yourself that are incongruent with everything else you are doing/saying, and every other way you present yourself, the anchoring you do will not overcome all those other signals. A man who is very bland and vanilla who self-points while talking about “dangerous, exciting men” is still not going to make her find him particularly ‘dangerous’ or ‘exciting’.

READ MORE: Being Yourself: How Important is Congruence?

Do your words, actions, and presentation align — or do they weirdly conflict?

However, if you anchor frames congruent with the way you’re presenting yourself and behaving around her, the anchoring only serves to strengthen those frames.

That is to say: if you are already acting like a sexy bad boy around her, and you anchor the frame of “exceptional lover” to yourself, that frame is generally going to stick.

 

Anchoring Emotions to Her

We don’t just self-point to create anchors, however. We can also other point.

What happens if you talk about “a girl in search of a good adventure” and point at her, then talk about “a man whose life is filled with adventure” as you self-point? Well, you’ll anchor the emotion of ‘looking for an adventure’ to her, in her mind, even as you anchor the emotion of ‘man capable of providing adventure’ to yourself, in her mind.

NLP seducers use entire routines to set these various frames and anchors. I won’t go into that here – but I do want you to understand the power of the self- and other points.

Let’s say you’ve got a girl at a bar who’s being resistant with you. She isn’t leaving, but she’s acting cagey and difficult whenever you talk to her. You decide to frame her as being difficult because she is horny, and yourself as a man able to resolve that issue for her. Here’s how that looks:

YOU: That seems like it’d be a challenging major.

HER: [stares at you a moment] I guess.

YOU: [pause] You know, sometimes at bars you run into someone who’s all wound up with pent up sexual tension. [gesture toward her] It’s pretty common; I mean, it’s why some people go to bars in the first place. Because at bars, you will also meet other folks who know how to resolve that tension [self-point] and are very good at it. Convenient thing, bars! Anyway, how’d you end up at this school in the middle of nowhere?

Use your gestures and anchor emotions where you want them.

While it seems like this bit of conversation comes out of nowhere, it’s actually prompted by her giving-you-nothing behavior. You don’t outright call her sexually pent-up, nor do you outright say that you’re a guy who can fix that for her. But by gesturing to her as you deliver one part of this short speech, and gesturing to yourself as you deliver another part of it, you get the message clearly across: “You are sexually pent up, but fortunately, you’ve run into the right guy.”

Then you switch topic right back to something in line with what you were discussing before the mini speech.

Can this work? I use this approach often with girls giving me some kind of resistance, combining a cold read about why I think she’s resisting me plus a vague statement about the reasons plus solution, made specific through self- and other points. The result is pretty much always that the girl warms up a lot right after.

How much of the warming up is due to you accurately reading where her head is at with your cold read?

How much of it is due to the frames you set, then anchor to herself and you?

I can’t say for sure, but I can tell you it works.

 

Pointing Away Negativity

Here’s a final tip (which I covered in my article on anchoring earlier), but any time boring or negative topics come up, if it’s something you have to address and cannot get off of, use distracted eye contact and gesture away from yourself (and the girl, unless you want to frame her as boring or negative for some reason, such as to tease her or put pressure on her to stop being that way).

The reason for this is that it anchors the negative, boring topics outside yourself and the girl – effectively exorcising them from your courtship.

 

Conclusion

You probably point sometimes without even realizing it.

Hand gestures are a natural part of human communication.

Yet by being more deliberate in your use of gestures, you can better anchor the frames and emotions you wish to create in your conversations with girls.

Try it out and see!

Chase

Title: How to Motivate Yourself to Pick Up Girls | Girls Chase
content:
You want women in your life but you can’t get off the couch. Are you lazy? Or are you just not doing what’s needed to MOTIVATE yourself to pick up girls?

We get guys periodically asking for help solving motivation issues around approaching and picking up women. Not the least of these being Sub-Zero, our long-time commenter who has long struggled with drive issues. Here’s a recent comment by him on the subject:

Actually getting some drive back, but still don’t have the drive to deal with everything that comes with the ups and downs of dating. I’m horny all the time and when I’m sleeping with women I’m always pleasing them, so I know that’s not the issue. I just don’t have the drive to keep going if things aren’t working out and quit. It makes me wonder how other guys can have no kind of success and can keep doing it. How do I get the drive to keep practicing and getting better instead of quitting?

All right then. Let’s talk about motivation.

I’ll see if I can come at it from a different angle than our many other articles on the subject.

First off, a couple of points:

This article is not a “you should be doing this” moral lecture. If you aren’t driven to approach or pick up girls, and you don’t want to be, that is fine. This guide is a tool, not  an order.

This article is also not a mandatory thing you have to follow even if you want to pick up. If you want to pick up girls, but just occasionally, and are happy with how it’s going, stick with it.

This article is for men who want MORE motivation to go out and approach more women but are struggling to find that motivation.

In other words, this is the article for men motivated to find the motivation to go out and pick up girls. Copy that?

 

The Spirit Is Willing but the Flesh Is Weak

What does it mean to wish you had the motivation to do something?

It’s a bit of a conundrum when you think about it:

Here is a man motivated to want to do something,

However, he is not sufficiently motivated to actually do it!

In fact, we encounter this ‘motivated to want to do what we aren’t motivated to actually do’ phenomenon in all kinds of things:

Wishing we had the motivation to kick a bad habit.

Wishing we had the motivation to set a new good habit.

Wishing we had the motivation to go out more and socialize.

Wishing we had the motivation to leave our current job.

Wishing we had the motivation to start our own business.

Wishing we had the motivation to exit a bad relationship.

Now, people work in different ways, and motivate themselves differently.

As the prison warden in 2002’s Count of Monte Cristo says (while noting the “God will grant me justice” inscription carved into the prison cell wall):

People are always looking to motivate themselves.

It’s true. We all wish we could somehow get ourselves to do more than we actually do.

The truth is, we are men, not machines. We cannot program ourselves to perform a desired function, then go out and mechanically execute it to perfection without resistance or fatigue.

We get tired. We get lazy. We lose focus. We lose interest.

We lose our motivation.

If we want ourselves to actually do what we want ourselves to do, then, we need to find a way around the inherent tendency of human beings (all living things, really) to avoid squandering energy on things that lack a guaranteed immediate payoff. We must instead lay a pathway for ourselves that gets us doing what we want to do.

 

Skill Builder Mentality
It’s time to level up like you’re a video game character.

I had a few false starts when it came to picking up girls.

There was when I was 17 years old, working in a department store, and I resolved to talk to at least one new girl a week – either another attractive coworker, a customer, or a girl I’d meet somewhere else in the mall. I managed to get a few approaches under my belt (even one upon the stunning girl who worked in the lingerie department!), but then I called it quits.

Then there was when I was 18 years old, down at the shore, with a whole plan about how I’d move there, get a job working at a restaurant, get an apartment, then hit the under-21 clubs every night dancing with girls until I figured out how to pick girls up. I went out a single night, got a few girls to dance with me, had a bunch more girls spurn me for dances, ended up sandwiched among a bunch of dancing, sweaty men, felt completely and utterly defeated, and threw in the towel on even trying to get girls for years.

It wasn’t until I was about to turn 22 that I finally learned to stick with it. I set a new approach goal – not every day; not even every week; just “approach three new girls” – and ended up hitting it… after a couple of months. Once I hit it, I set some new goals: next, instead of just approach, I’d ask girls for their phone numbers. Some girls told me no, but rather than a rejection beating me down like rejections had when I was 18, the very fact that I’d gone for a goal (even if I failed to reach it) encouraged me.

Then one day I got a number that was good. I went on a date. I went on more. I started going out more and talking to more women, then more. I learned how to pick girls up for one-night stands from nightclubs. I got a rotation going of girls I was seeing. I had friends with benefits. I took girlfriends.

As I progressed, I continued to set more goals: could I pick up girls from social circle? Could I pick up girls from day game? Could I pick up from the street, train, supermarket, library, park, you name it? Could I get hotter girls? Could I get girls with really big boobs? Could I get stunners with consistency? (answer to all of those: yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, and yes)

Why was I able to stick with it at 22 when I’d failed to do so when I’d tried it at 17 and 18?

A big part of what was missing was the correct skill progression to keep me motivated.

As a 17-year-old, I figured I’d talk to girls until I was able to get a date. But when I approached girls, I discovered just how far I was from being able to get dates. Like that stunner in the lingerie department – we had a very nice, platonic conversation that I knew had a 0% chance of ever leading to a date. Later I saw her going around with some guy on her lunch break. A date? A boyfriend? I figured I’d keep an eye on her and chat her up again a few months later – maybe she’d be single. This was the WRONG mentality. I was going for dates – I wasn’t going for skills.

As an 18-year-old, I’d realized I needed to skill-build, but I had an overly simplistic idea about what that’d be like. Sure, at first I figured I’d need to commit to months of going out and probably doing awful at the beginning, but I’d had limited real experience with girls rejecting me, and that first night out piling up a bunch of rejections hit like a ton of bricks. I was unprepared for it; it crushed my pride, and the whole plan of going out and doing that again night after night folded.

At last, as a 22-year-old, I came at it the right way:

I’d set small, achievable goals, aimed at inching my way toward greater success with women, until I’d arrived at a place where I could reliably get girls.

READ MORE: Goal Setting

Set goals — then hit them.

 

Small Goals Work Because They’re Rewarding
Basic fetch quests are a staple of skill progression in many role-playing games.

If you’ve ever played a really absorbing video game, and paid attention to how the game absorbed you, you will have noticed it went something like this:

At the start of the game, you had a very simple task to complete. You completed it and the game rewarded you.

Then you received another task to complete, this one slightly more complicated. Again, you completed it, and again the game rewarded you.

Next, you received another task, once again a bit more challenging than the last, but well within the ability of your growing skill set. Once again, you completed it, and the game rewarded you.

Most of your favorite games likely feature this smooth gradual escalation in challenges and rewards, which teach you over time how to play the game. You get into it, get hooked, have a hard time not playing, and get better and better at the game as you play.

A good set of goals in pickup is just like this. It consists of a series of achievable goals that escalate in challenge as you go, but never beyond the limit of what is doable for you.

One of the reasons students are ecstatic with me when I coach them to pick up girls in-field is because I construct game-like series of escalating goals or quests for them as we go through a session. Even a guy who has never approached a girl before can end up leaving with phone numbers or a girl on his arm when we do this because the right series of rapidly achievable ‘seduction quest’ milestones for a student allow him to progress rapidly in a one-on-one session.

Just like in a video game, you don’t tell the student all the upcoming quests ahead of time (that’d be overwhelming and get him in his head); you just tell him the current one. Then after he completes it, you assign him his next. Then his next. Before he knows it he’s doing stuff he's never done with girls before, beyond what he thought he was capable of doing, and he is hooked.

You can do this exact same thing to yourself, without a coach standing over your shoulder, IF you have the sense to do it. All you need to do is sit down for a few minutes and ask yourself, “What is the next small step I need to learn how to take with girls?” and that becomes your target.

You must do this regularly, or else you get trapped too long repeating the same ‘quest’ again and again. After you collect enough wolf hides in the video game, you don’t want to go back and keep collecting more wolf hides, because the XP gain is no longer very much. You need to move to a more challenging quest. So too with girls.

You learned how to approach, open, and banter? Great! But don’t limit yourself to just continuing to do that over and over then eject. You need to learn how to move girls next. You need to learn how to get some initial bonding going. You need to learn how to create high points so you can ask girls out.

 

Main Story Quest Goal vs. Tasks & Side Quests

A lot of guys get confused, then deflated, with seduction because they only focus on the Main Story Quest Goal of seduction. Depending on the guy, that typically comes down to some variation of ‘Get the Girl’ (or ‘Get Many Girls’, as the case may be!).

But if that is the only thing a guy focuses his energy on, it’s well nigh unachievable. It’d be like starting a big game, receiving the quest of “Save the Entire World”, except you are a super weak Level 1 character with no skills or abilities who dies fast, you have no idea what to do, and because there are no smaller quests or tasks to guide you, you just can’t get anywhere. People get very frustrated with games like this and quit them quick because they feel too unrewarding.

So too with seduction where guys only focus on the Main Story Quest Goal of ‘Get the Girl / Many Girls’. A guy will go out, chat up a few chicks, NOT get the girl, let alone MANY girls, feel like he’s failed, feel totally lost and unguided, feel completely unrewarded for his efforts, and soon give up.

Humans only stick with things that reward them. Just like an absorbing computer game, you have to set up a series of achievable seduction tasks to make your learning process rewarding to you.

You can have that Main Story Quest Goal of ‘Get the Girl’ in the back of your mind; that is fine.

But just like in a game, your immediate focus will not be that Main Story Quest Goal.

Instead, it will be the far more immediately achievable minor task or side quest that lies right in front of you – those achievable, bite-sized goals you lay out for yourself.

 

No More AFC Material

There’s another side to motivating yourself to pick up girls, too, and that is believing that you can actually do it. The rewarding progress you feel hitting goal after goal will help. But only if it isn’t being cancelled out by the media you consume.

All of us are deeply influenced by media we consume. The only time we aren’t is when our experience is so deep and broad that we know the things the media says are balderdash. The rest of the time, whatever we hear through our ears and see through our eyes gets added into our mental models of the world.

READ MORE: Mind Control: How Media Influence Your Thoughts and Feelings

Don’t let the media tell you what to believe.

The vast majority of men who create media are Average Frustrated Chumps. This goes doubly so for the men who churn out red pill, black pill, and incel media.

Yes, in the beginning, there were some skilled pick up artists and seducers involved in the red pill movement. These men were quickly pushed aside as the movement became a mass movement and bitter men flooded in en masse. Remember when “don’t talk about fight club” was the mantra of the pickup artist community, and one of the best known PUAs called himself Tyler Durden? Now the ‘fight club’ meme is tied to the cheesy mainstream-ish platitudes of the red pill and is all played out. Sad days!

Sub-Zero, our commenter we started this article with, has made repeated reference in his comments on Girls Chase articles about the messages he gets from AFC red pill influencers, which he says confuse him. Girls Chase says this, but AFCs say that. Who is correct?

Here’s the deal: if a guy isn’t getting what he wants in life, he’s average, and he’s frustrated, and he’s a chump. If a guy is going onto media and complaining up, down, left, right, and center about women, he is not getting what he wants with women, and he is an Average Frustrated Chump. If you are listening to all this Average Frustrated Chump media, and you are letting this stuff into your brain, and you are wondering if it might be correct, you are letting it turn you into an Average Frustrated Chump.

I can watch AFC media and have it wash right over me. I can listen to these guys spout out “their truths” about “modern women” and I know it’s bunk because I have enough experience with modern women to know these guys have a.) picked BADLY and b.) run their relationships BADLY. Furthermore, I know that if these guys were getting laid a lot, and not going for the broken chicks they are going for, and running their relationships with a modicum of skill, they would not be dealing with the problems they complain about constantly with women, because nobody who is doing things correctly has to deal with these things – at least not to the extent where it’s screwing the guy’s life up utterly like these guys’ lives are screwed up.

Almost every single man producing red pill or black pill media today is an Average Frustrated Chump. Men who consume this stuff fill their heads with mental models downloaded from Average Frustrated Chumps. If you want to be an AFC, the easiest way in the world is to listen to AFC music, watch AFC movies, suck up AFC podcasts, then go out into the world and think, feel, and act like all the AFC stuff you have downloaded into your skull.

I have even seen with skilled pickup artists who got away from the game for a bit, then started consuming heaps of AFC material, that they reverted to AFC mentalities and started complaining about all these AFC complaints. Whenever this has happened and I have asked the guy, “Hey man, I respect you a lot, and you had a lot of experience in the past – but are you in the field right now or is this coming from media you consume?” the answer is always the same: the guy is not in the field right now and is just consuming media.

THE MEDIA LIES TO YOU. It is filled with people with extremely limited experience, who are living in their heads, concocting schemes and hypothesis based on their imaginations, remixing ideas they picked up from other men living in their own heads, creating this entire fabricated reality of nonsense and unreality.

READ MORE: Are You Free or Do the Glowing Screens Direct You?

You are not truly free if the screens you look at program you.

The less you are out in the real world interacting with flesh and blood women and actually having deep and involved relationships with them – having deep flirtations, deep connections, going on dates, getting intimate with them, having relationships with them, and doing this often, not occasionally – the more susceptible you will be to having your mind filled with propaganda broadcast out of AFCs online.

If you consume AFC material, unless you are KNEE DEEP IN THE FIELD, you will become more and more like an AFC.

Reading Girls Chase while also consuming a bunch of AFC material is not enough to inoculate yourself against this stuff. In theory, if you are reading Girls Chase, plus heavily in the field, you should be able to consume a bunch of AFC material and not have it affect you. However, in practice, as soon as you are in the field a lot, having lots of actual experience with women, and progressing through game (hopefully helped along by stuff you are learning from the Girls Chase website, and/or my book, and/or One Date/TDA), you will not have an appetite for AFC rants and lamentations anymore.

Instead, you will just turn them on, find their perspectives extremely average, find the frustration in them grating, and view the guys spouting these perspectives as chumps – then you will turn that media off.

You should not be consuming this stuff AT ALL when you are trying to motivate yourself. It is anti-motivational. It is motivation-destroying.

Listening to some guy rant about how there are no good women left, or women are all raging sluts, or women only want men with 10/10 male model looks, or whatever AFC tripe a guy is consuming, is only going to deflate you.

You listen to that blather, and what’s the point of even trying with girls?

Why would you bother if “women only want men who are young, rich, good-looking, tall, and famous?” That excludes 99.999% of the male population – including you, me, every guy I know who is actually good with girls, and everybody else. There are like 3 guys who are getting all the girls according to this AFC claptrap. So what’s the point? If you’re not one of those 3 guys, sorry, all the girls on Planet Earth don’t want you. Does that sound reasonable?

You’ve gotta tune that stuff out.

If it’s so important for you to listen to, you are not ready to motivate yourself to pick up girls.

YOU MUST CHOOSE:

Fill your mind with anti-motivational victim mentality crap, or turn that AFC bullshit off and go get good with girls.

Your choice, hombre.

 

Axing Out AFC Friends/Associates
They may be great guys, but they are not going to help your dating life.

Finally, this is not a problem I’ve had to deal with myself (largely because I didn’t have friends, really, when I started on this journey; and since then I’ve only kept friends around who were cool and good with girls), but I have had multiple guys tell me about this:
